passage:
Maple Court Shared Flats: House Rules for Tenants

A  Rent and bills. Rent is due on the first day of each month and should be paid by bank transfer. Electricity, water and internet are included in the rent, but tenants who use portable heaters will be charged an extra fee during the winter months. Please report any problems with payments to the office before the due date.

B  Kitchen and shared areas. Each tenant has one shelf in the fridge and one cupboard. Please wash and put away your dishes within two hours of cooking. The cleaning rota is displayed on the kitchen door; every tenant is responsible for cleaning the kitchen and bathroom once every three weeks. Food left in the fridge after the end of a tenancy will be thrown away.

C  Visitors. Tenants may have guests at any time, but overnight guests may stay for a maximum of three nights in any one month. Please inform your flatmates in advance if someone will be staying. Guests must not be given keys to the building.

D  Noise. Quiet hours are from 11 p.m. to 7 a.m. on weekdays and from midnight to 8 a.m. at weekends. Please use headphones when listening to music or watching films late in the evening. Parties are not permitted in the flats under any circumstances.

E  Repairs and maintenance. Report any repairs through the online form on the tenants' website. Emergency repairs, such as a burst pipe or a total loss of power, should be reported by telephone to the 24-hour line. Tenants must not attempt to repair electrical equipment themselves. Staff will give at least 24 hours' notice before entering a flat, except in an emergency.

F  Bicycles and rubbish. Bicycles must be kept in the locked shed behind the building and not in corridors or stairways. Recycling bins are collected on Tuesdays and general waste on Fridays.

passage:
Moving Out: A Guide to Getting Your Deposit Back

A  When you rent a property, you will normally be asked to pay a deposit, often equivalent to four or five weeks' rent. This money is held as security in case you damage the property or fail to pay the rent. In many places, landlords are legally required to protect the deposit in an approved scheme, and you should receive written confirmation of this within a few weeks of paying it.

B  The most important document at the end of a tenancy is the inventory. This is a detailed list, usually with photographs, describing the condition of the property and its contents when you moved in. If you did not receive an inventory, take your own dated photographs as soon as possible after moving in and send copies to your landlord or agent by email, so that there is a record of when they were taken.

C  Landlords may deduct money from your deposit for damage, unpaid rent or cleaning if the property is less clean than when you moved in. However, they cannot charge you for 'fair wear and tear', which means the gradual deterioration that results from normal use. A carpet that has become slightly worn after several years is an example of fair wear and tear; a large burn mark is not.

D  Before you leave, clean the property thoroughly, including inside the oven and fridge, and remove all of your belongings. Return every key, including spare keys for windows and the post box. Attend the check-out inspection if you can, and take your own photographs on the day you leave. Make sure your landlord has your new address.

E  If your landlord proposes deductions that you think are unfair, first try to reach an agreement by discussing the matter politely and providing evidence. If this fails, deposit protection schemes offer a free dispute resolution service, in which an independent adjudicator examines the evidence from both sides and makes a decision. Using this service does not require you to go to court.

explanation: 第C段落で fair wear and tear（通常使用による劣化）は請求できないとあるので FALSE。

NOTICE TO ALL STAFF: Changes to the Staff Canteen from 3 March

A  Following the results of last autumn's staff survey, we are making several changes to the canteen on the ground floor of the main building. We hope these will make lunchtimes quicker and give everyone a wider choice of food.

B  New opening hours. The canteen will open at 7.30 a.m. for breakfast, half an hour earlier than at present, and hot food will be served until 2.30 p.m. Sandwiches, salads and drinks will remain available from the self-service counter until 4 p.m. The canteen will continue to close at weekends.

C  Payment. From 3 March, the canteen will no longer accept cash. Staff can pay using a bank card, a mobile phone or their staff ID card, which can be topped up at the machine beside the entrance. Staff who pay with their ID card will receive a 10% discount on all hot meals.

D  Menu. A vegetarian main course will now be available every day, and a vegan option will be offered on Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays. The weekly menu will be sent to all staff by email every Friday afternoon. Information about allergens is available from the serving staff, who can also show you the full list of ingredients for each dish.

E  Seating. To reduce queues and crowding between 12.30 and 1.30 p.m., the meeting room next to the canteen will be available as extra seating during that hour. Please remember to return trays to the racks near the exit. Comments and suggestions can be left in the box by the till or sent to the facilities team.

Staff Canteen: Food Allergies and Special Diets

A  Our commitment. The canteen team wants every member of staff to be able to eat safely. All of our dishes are prepared in the canteen kitchen by our own chefs, and we label every dish on the counter with the main allergens it contains.

B  What you should do. If you have a food allergy, please tell the serving staff each time you order, even if you eat in the canteen regularly. Recipes and suppliers sometimes change, and staff on duty may differ from day to day. Do not rely only on the labels, as these show the main allergens but not every ingredient.

C  Limits. Our kitchen handles nuts, sesame, gluten, milk and eggs. Although we take great care to keep ingredients separate, we cannot guarantee that any dish is completely free from traces of these allergens. Staff with severe allergies may prefer to bring their own food, and a microwave and fridge are available in the staff kitchen on the second floor for this purpose.

D  Special diets. If you follow a diet for medical or religious reasons, you can ask the head chef, Mr Okonkwo, to prepare a suitable meal. Please give at least two working days' notice so that ingredients can be ordered. There is no extra charge for this service.

Staff with allergies only need to inform the canteen once.
explanation: Section B に毎回注文のたびに伝えるようにとあるので FALSE。

Riverside College: Short Courses This Spring

A  Introduction to Bookkeeping. Learn how to record income and expenses, prepare simple accounts and use common spreadsheet functions. Ideal for people running a small business. Eight Tuesday evenings, starting 4 April. A certificate is awarded to students who complete a short final assignment.

B  Conversational Spanish for Beginners. No previous knowledge is needed. Classes focus on speaking and listening in everyday situations such as shopping, ordering food and asking for directions. Ten Thursday evenings. The textbook is included in the course fee.

Diploma in Hospitality Management (One Year, Full-Time)

A  This practical diploma prepares students for supervisory and management roles in hotels, restaurants, event venues and tourist attractions. It combines classroom study with substantial work experience, and is designed for school leavers as well as people who already work in the industry and wish to progress.

B  Course content. Students study six core modules: customer service, food and beverage operations, accommodation management, marketing, finance for hospitality and managing people. In the second semester, students choose one specialist module from either event planning or sustainable tourism.

C  Work placement. All students complete a ten-week paid placement with one of our partner employers. Placements are arranged by the college's careers team, although students may suggest their own employer if it meets our requirements. Students who are already employed in the industry may be able to complete the placement at their current workplace.

D  Assessment. There are no written examinations. Instead, students are assessed through practical tasks, reports, presentations and a final project in which they plan and run a real event for the local community.

E  Entry requirements. Applicants should normally have completed secondary education. Those without formal qualifications but with at least two years' relevant work experience are also welcome to apply and will be invited to an interview. Applicants whose first language is not English need an IELTS score of 5.5 or equivalent.
